text:
maya: Ran a focused scheduler sweep on staging (16x A10s) for microbatch sizing and kernel routing. Quick TL;DR: p95 improved a bit, p99 tail got worse and correlates with KV hit drops during short bursts. dump below.

alex: numbers plz — what configs did you change?

maya: baseline vs sweep (30m windows, mixed short/long seq workload):
```
baseline cfg: max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=10, microbatch_target=256
baseline perf: p50=34ms, p95=138ms, p99=412ms, tokens/s=9.2k, kv_hit=0.41

sweep cfg: max_batch_tokens=1024, max_wait_ms=14, microbatch_target=128, kernel_routing=adaptive
sweep perf: p50=30ms, p95=123ms, p99=520ms, tokens/s=8.0k, kv_hit=0.27
```

maya: So p95 ~15ms better, but p99 +108ms and throughput dropped ~13%. KV hit rate fell from 41% -> 27% during the peak — looks like more short requests forced smaller batches that evicted prefixes more often and caused more cold KV lookups.

dev-bot: profiling link: https://perf.internal/redwood/staging/1998765432 — flamegraph shows spikes at kernel_fallback_path and nvtx:kv_load for the tail samples :warning:

samir: interesting. kernel_routing=adaptive probably pushed some sequences onto the slower fp32 fallback because microbatches had odd length distributions. do we have seq-length histogram?

maya: yes — attached hist (summary): 60% short (<64), 30% mid (64-512), 10% long (>512). When max_batch_tokens lowered, scheduler favored reducing wait and sent many short requests through quickly -> more small microbatches, which bumped some mid-length sequences into fallback path due to kernel-selection thresholds.

nina: saw logs showing kernel fallback triggered at these conditions:
```
[2026-03-15T12:17:23Z] kernel_router: selected=quantized_fast, fallback=fp32_kernel, reason=seq_len_bucket_mismatch, microbatch=3, total_tokens=142
[2026-03-15T12:17:23Z] kv: miss=true, prefix_evicted=true, kv_load_ms=48
```

nina: so smaller microbatches increased eviction pressure on the KV cache (prefix windows are per-GPU), causing more misses which amplify p99.

alex: makes sense. two levers here: raise max_batch_tokens to reduce kv churn or increase max_wait_ms to let the scheduler build larger batches. Both will increase p95 slightly but could tame the p99. any tradeoffs on throughput/cost?

maya: short note: increasing max_wait_ms from 10->20 (without touching max_batch_tokens) in a quick probe: p95 +8ms, p99 -60ms, tokens/s -4%. Increasing max_batch_tokens to 3072: p95 -2ms, p99 -30ms, tokens/s +2% (but kernel routing had fewer fallbacks). So increasing max_batch_tokens helped more than bumping wait in this workload.

samir: surprising that larger max_batch_tokens reduced p95 in that test. probably because it allowed different kernel selection heuristics to use the faster kernels for mid-length sequences (fewer fallbacks).

ops-bot: alert suppressed: staging KV eviction spikes observed during sweep window (root cause: microbatch sizing).

maya: proposed next actions:
- run A/B (15m each) on staging comparing: A) max_batch_tokens=3072, max_wait_ms=10 vs B) max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=18
- enable kv-prefetching (experimental flag) on B to see if prefetch offsets eviction hits
- add a targeted profiler: log kernel selection reason + kv_hit boolean for any request with latency > p99_threshold

nina: +1 on targeted profiler. Also add metric: per-gpu prefix_eviction_rate; we need to know if it's skewed to specific GPUs.

alex: will spin up the A/B run. tagging @infra to reserve GPUs for the test window.

samir: if A wins we should consider raising default max_batch_tokens for this instance type, but also add a safe guard: if kv_hit < 0.2, auto-relax batch size to avoid tail regressions.

maya: agreed. I'll open a short RFC/ops runbook with the experiment plan and the telemetry queries. putting a placeholder jira: RW-3371.

dev-bot: created task RW-3371 and attached perf snapshots. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks — let’s reconvene after the A/B. if p99 still noisy we can try a hybrid: per-route max_wait_ms tuned by sequence-length classifier.

maya: noted. thanks all. :raised_hands:
